nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid, $k$ a natural number and $x = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ a sequence in $M$. For every $j < 2^k$, the value at position $j$ of Blelloch's scan of $x$ on $2^k$ positions is the exclusive prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{j-1}$ (equal to $1$ when $j = 0$).
nodes.title: Blelloch's scan computes the exclusive prefix products

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid. For a natural number $k$ and a list $xs = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ in $M$, the list scan $L_k(xs)$ is defined by recursion on $k$: $L_0(xs)$ is the one-element list $(1)$, and $L_{k+1}(xs)$ is obtained from the list scan $z = L_k(p)$ of the pair products $p = (x_0 x_1, x_2 x_3, \dots)$ of $xs$ (a trailing unpaired entry is dropped) by interleaving: $L_{k+1}(xs) = (z_0, z_0 x_0, z_1, z_1 x_2, \dots)$,…
nodes.title: Blelloch's scan on lists

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, the span of Blelloch's scan on $n = 2^k$ positions is $2k = 2 \log_2 n$.
nodes.title: Blelloch's scan has logarithmic span

nodes.summary: The span $S(k)$ of Blelloch's scan on $2^k$ positions is defined by $S(0) = 0$ and $S(k+1) = S(k) + 2$: one parallel step for the pair products, the recursive scan, and one parallel step for the odd positions.
nodes.title: Parallel steps of Blelloch's scan

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k$, the number $W(k)$ of monoid multiplications Blelloch's scan performs on $n = 2^k$ positions satisfies $W(k) + 2 = 2^{k+1}$, so $W(k) = 2^{k+1} - 2 < 2n$.
nodes.title: Blelloch's scan is work-efficient

nodes.summary: The number $W(k)$ of monoid multiplications Blelloch's scan performs on $2^k$ positions is defined by $W(0) = 0$ and $W(k+1) = 2^k + W(k) + 2^k$: on $2^{k+1}$ positions, $2^k$ pair products, the recursive scan on the $2^k$ pair products, and $2^k$ products for the odd positions.
nodes.title: Work of Blelloch's scan

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid. For a natural number $k$ and a sequence $x = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ in $M$, the scan $B_k(x)$ is the sequence in $M$ defined by recursion on $k$: $B_0(x)$ is constantly $1$, and $B_{k+1}(x)$ is obtained from the scan $y = B_k(p)$ of the pair products $p_i = x_{2i} x_{2i+1}$ by setting $B_{k+1}(x)_{2i} = y_i$ and $B_{k+1}(x)_{2i+1} = y_i x_{2i}$ for every $i$.
nodes.title: Blelloch's scan

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid. For lists $z = (z_0, z_1, \dots)$ and $x = (x_0, x_1, \dots)$ in $M$, the expansion of $z$ along $x$ is the list $(z_0, z_0 x_0, z_1, z_1 x_2, z_2, z_2 x_4, \dots)$: each $z_i$ is followed by $z_i x_{2i}$, and the list stops at the first $i$ for which $z_i$ or $x_{2i+1}$ does not exist.
nodes.title: Interleaving step of Blelloch's list scan

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid, $k$ a natural number and $xs = (x_0, \dots, x_{2^k - 1})$ a list in $M$ of length $2^k$. For every $j < 2^k$, the entry at position $j$ of Blelloch's list scan of $xs$ in $k$ rounds is the exclusive prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_{j-1}$ (equal to $1$ when $j = 0$).
nodes.title: The list implementation computes the exclusive prefix products

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid, $k$ a natural number and $xs = (x_0, \dots, x_{2^k - 1})$ a list in $M$ of length $2^k$. For every $j < 2^k$, the entry at position $j$ of Blelloch's list scan of $xs$ in $k$ rounds equals the value at position $j$ of Blelloch's scan on $2^k$ positions of the sequence $x_0, \dots, x_{2^k - 1}, 1, 1, \dots$ obtained by extending $xs$ by $1$.
nodes.title: The list implementation computes Blelloch's scan

nodes.summary: Let $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ be a list of elements of a monoid $M$ and let $K$ be a natural number with $n \le 2^K$. Then for every $i < n$, entry $i$ of the list produced by $K$ rounds of the tabulated scan equals the prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_i$.
nodes.title: The tabulated scan computes all prefix products

nodes.summary: Let $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$ be a list of elements of a monoid $M$, extended to a sequence by $x_j = 1$ for $j \ge n$. For every number of rounds $K$ and every position $i < n$, entry $i$ of the list produced by $K$ rounds of the tabulated scan equals the value at position $i$ after $K$ rounds of the Kogge–Stone scan applied to the sequence $x$.
nodes.title: The tabulated scan agrees with the round recursion

nodes.summary: Let $x_0, x_1, \dots$ be a sequence in a monoid $M$ and let $n$ be a natural number. After $\lceil \log_2 n \rceil$ rounds of the Kogge–Stone scan (the least $K$ with $n \le 2^K$), every position $i < n$ holds the prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_i$.
nodes.title: The scan computes all prefixes in logarithmically many rounds

nodes.summary: Let $x_0, x_1, \dots$ be a sequence in a monoid $M$ and let $n$ and $K$ be natural numbers with $n \le 2^K$. After $K$ rounds of the Kogge–Stone scan, every position $i < n$ holds the prefix product $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_i$.
nodes.title: The scan computes all prefix products

nodes.summary: Let $x_0, x_1, \dots$ be a sequence in a monoid $M$, let $k$ and $i$ be natural numbers, and let $m = \min(i + 1, 2^k)$. After $k$ rounds of the Kogge–Stone scan, position $i$ holds the product $x_{i+1-m} \cdots x_i$ of the $m$ consecutive inputs ending at $i$, taken in increasing order of index.
nodes.title: What the scan holds after each round

nodes.summary: Given a sequence $x_0, x_1, \dots$ in a monoid $M$, the value $s_k(i)$ at position $i$ after $k$ rounds is defined by $s_0(i) = x_i$ and, for each $k$, $s_{k+1}(i) = s_k(i - 2^k) \, s_k(i)$ if $2^k \le i$ and $s_{k+1}(i) = s_k(i)$ otherwise.
nodes.title: The Kogge–Stone scan

nodes.summary: For a list $[a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_{n-1}]$ of elements of a monoid $M$, the list of adjacent pair products is $[a_0 a_1, a_2 a_3, \ldots]$: it has length $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$, its $i$-th entry is $a_{2i} a_{2i+1}$, and when $n$ is odd the last element $a_{n-1}$ is dropped.
nodes.title: Adjacent pair products of a list

nodes.summary: For a sequence $x \colon \mathbb{N} \to M$ in a monoid $M$, the sequence of adjacent pair products is the sequence whose term at $i$ is $x(2i) \cdot x(2i+1)$.
nodes.title: Adjacent pair products of a sequence

nodes.summary: For a sequence $x_0, x_1, \dots$ in a monoid $M$ and a natural number $i$, the prefix product at $i$ is $x_0 x_1 \cdots x_i$, the factors taken in increasing order of index.
nodes.title: Prefix product

nodes.summary: Given a list $y_0, \dots, y_{n-1}$ in a monoid $M$ and a natural number $k$, one round produces the list of length $n$ whose entry $i$ is $y_{i - 2^k} \, y_i$ when $2^k \le i$ and $y_i$ when $i < 2^k$.
nodes.title: One round of the scan on a list

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the work of round $k$ on $n$ positions equals the number of positions $i$ with $2^k \le i < n$.
nodes.title: The work of a round counts its combining positions

nodes.summary: The work of round $k$ on $n$ positions is $\max(n - 2^k, 0)$, the number of positions $i < n$ with $i \ge 2^k$, each of which performs one multiplication.
nodes.title: Work of a scan round

nodes.summary: For a list $y = (y_0, \dots, y_{n-1})$ in a monoid $M$, the list after $K$ rounds is defined by recursion on $K$: after $0$ rounds it is $y$, and after $K + 1$ rounds it is round $K$ applied to the list after $K$ rounds. Here round $k$ sends a list $(z_0, \dots, z_{n-1})$ to the list of length $n$ whose entry $i$ is $z_i$ for $i < 2^k$ and $z_{i - 2^k} z_i$ for $2^k \le i < n$.
nodes.title: Tabulated Kogge–Stone scan

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a monoid and $x : \mathbb{N} \to M$ a sequence, and for $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$ let $x_{[a, b)}$ be the ordered product $x_a x_{a+1} \cdots x_{b-1}$ (equal to $1$ if $b \le a$). For all $a \le b \le c$, $x_{[a, b)} \, x_{[b, c)} = x_{[a, c)}$.
nodes.title: Products of adjacent windows

nodes.summary: For a sequence $x : \mathbb{N} \to M$ in a monoid $M$ and $a, b \in \mathbb{N}$, the window product is the ordered product $x_a x_{a+1} \cdots x_{b-1}$ of the terms with indices $a \le j < b$; it is the empty product $1$ when $b \le a$.
nodes.title: Window product

nodes.summary: The span of $K$ rounds of the scan is $K$: each round is one parallel step.
nodes.title: Span of the Kogge–Stone scan

nodes.summary: For all $n, K \in \mathbb{N}$, the total work of $K$ rounds of the scan on $n$ positions is at most $nK$.
nodes.title: Work bound for the Kogge–Stone scan

nodes.summary: The total work of $K$ rounds on $n$ positions is $\sum_{k=0}^{K-1} \max(n - 2^k, 0)$, the sum over the rounds $k < K$ of the work $\max(n - 2^k, 0)$ of round $k$.
nodes.title: Work of the Kogge–Stone scan

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
